evals.name: adopt-with-existing-setup
evals.prompt: Can you onboard this repo onto our team setup? AGENTS.md for the agent rules with CLAUDE.md importing it, `make check` as the gate, our git hooks, CODEOWNERS. Don't clobber anything that's already here.
evals.expected_output: AGENTS.md is added, written for this repository (Node ESM, no dependencies, its commands and its money and migration rules), and CLAUDE.md imports it with an @AGENTS.md line while keeping every rule of its hand-written list; make check now runs what CI runs (lint, the node tests with the test job's FULL_PROPERTY_TESTS=1 so all 7 pass and none is skipped, migration check) under CI's TZ=UTC and passes on a machine in another zone, where the fixture's check ran lint only despite the README's claim; the time-zone dependence of the tests is reported, not patched in src/; the team's tools/githooks pre-commit keeps running because core.hooksPath is not repointed without chaining it; no hook the run writes, pre-commit included, refuses what the team does today or anything else (every subject in the history, including an 89-character Conventional one, direct commits on main, empty and reword commits) without saying so; the real owners in .gitlab/CODEOWNERS are not shadowed; anything shared under .claude/ is not swallowed by the `.claude/` ignore; the uncommitted edit in src/invoice.js is left alone and reported; only the requested pieces are added; nothing is committed and no GitHub files land in a GitLab repository.
expectations: AGENTS.md exists at the repository root and is written for this repository: it names its real gate and commands (make check, npm test or the like, none invented), says it is a dependency-free Node ESM service, and carries or points to its domain rules (integer paise, basis-point GST rates, append-only migrations); it holds no rule for a language or tool the repository does not use (for example TypeScript rules or pnpm)

CLAUDE.md contains a line that is exactly `@AGENTS.md` (Claude Code's import syntax; a markdown link or a sentence pointing at AGENTS.md does not load it), and every rule in the fixture's CLAUDE.md list "Things Claude gets wrong here" survives, with its meaning intact, in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md: money is integer paise with no floats or toFixed, GST rates are basis points, migrations are append-only, and gstPaise rounds half up and must not be changed to banker's rounding

`make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository with the uncommitted src/invoice.js edit present and TZ=Asia/Kolkata in the environment (CI pins TZ: "UTC" in .gitlab-ci.yml; test/fiscal.test.js fails under any zone east of UTC+4)

`make check` runs all three things .gitlab-ci.yml runs, under CI's TZ=UTC: the lint, the node tests and the migration check (npm run check:migrations); at the fixture state `check: lint` ran the lint only

`make check` runs the node tests with the test job's own variable FULL_PROPERTY_TESTS=1 (set on the job in .gitlab-ci.yml, not at the top level): when the grader runs `make check` with FULL_PROPERTY_TESTS unset in the environment, the test run executes all 7 tests with 0 skipped and 0 failed, however the counts are printed; a run that executes 6 and skips the property test is passing on less than CI checks

The final message says that the fixture's make check ran only the lint, so the README's claim that make check runs everything CI runs was false, or the run shows the README claim is now true and says what changed

src/fiscal.js and the tests are not changed to get the gate green, and the final message reports that the test suite depends on the process time zone (CI pins TZ=UTC; on this machine's zone the financialYear boundary test fails without it)

The Makefile's existing targets help, setup, dev, lint and test still exist and do what they did (setup still configures the hooks the team uses); no target was deleted or replaced wholesale. Giving an existing target the variables CI sets for the same step (TZ=UTC, FULL_PROPERTY_TESTS=1 on test) counts as doing what it did, not as a change

After the run, a commit in this clone would still run the team's tools/githooks/pre-commit (the append-only migration guard, lint and migration check): core.hooksPath is still tools/githooks, or it points somewhere whose pre-commit calls tools/githooks/pre-commit; and `make setup` configures the same hooks path the clone now has
tools/githooks/pre-commit is not deleted or weakened: the check that refuses modified or deleted files under migrations/ is still there

Any new hook the run adds is either actually run by git on this clone (reachable through core.hooksPath or called from tools/githooks) or the final message states plainly that it is not active yet and gives the exact step to wire it in; a hook written to a directory git does not read and reported as installed fails this

Every commit-msg hook the run writes, whether or not git runs it yet, accepts every subject in the fixture history, which the grader feeds to it one at a time as a message file: `feat: invoice totals with GST in paise`, `feat: POST /totals and line items table`, `chore: team pre-commit hook, make setup, Claude notes` and the 89-character `test(money): check half-up GST rounding over 20000 amounts in CI with FULL_PROPERTY_TESTS`; or the final message names each rejected subject and the rule that rejects it as a change the team must agree to

Every pre-push hook the run writes, active or not, accepts what the team does today: a push from main straight to main, branch names with no task id, no terminal confirmation, and a push that sends no new commits (for example a tag on an already-pushed commit). And no new hook of any kind (pre-commit, commit-msg or pre-push) refuses anything the final message does not name: a subject length limit, an em dash rule on staged prose or a staged-credential scan each counts as a refusal that must be named

If git on this clone runs any pre-commit hook the run added (directly or chained from tools/githooks), an intentional empty commit (`git commit --allow-empty -m "chore: probe"`) and a reword of the last commit with nothing staged (`--amend -m "chore: reworded probe"`) both still succeed. The grader tries both in a copy of the output repository; where it cannot run git commit there, invoking every active pre-commit and commit-msg hook the way git would, with an empty index and each message, is the accepted equivalent. A hook that refuses a commit because nothing is staged fails this

The owners in .gitlab/CODEOWNERS are unchanged and still take effect: the run adds no CODEOWNERS at the repository root or in docs/, which GitLab would read instead of .gitlab/CODEOWNERS, and no placeholder handle such as @lead or @engineering becomes an effective owner

No file the run adds under .claude/ for the team to share is ignored by git (the fixture's .gitignore ignores all of `.claude/` at line 4; the grader checks with git check-ignore), or the run adds nothing under .claude/; if the ignore is narrowed, .claude/settings.local.json stays ignored

The uncommitted edit to src/invoice.js (the WIP discountPaise parameter) is still in the working tree, unchanged and uncommitted, not reverted, stashed or folded into other changes, and the final message mentions that the tree had an uncommitted change; the run makes no git commit (history still ends at the fixture's fourth commit, no new stash entries) and leaves the commit to the engineer

The run adds nothing the request did not ask for beyond what those pieces need: no SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, .editorconfig, docs/ templates, issue or merge request templates, no .github/ directory (the repository is on GitLab), and no CI change, where changing a package.json script that CI calls (test, lint, check:migrations) counts as a CI change; package.json gains no dependency, the existing .gitignore entries (node_modules/, coverage/, .env) are all still present and .claude/settings.local.json is not created; any shared Claude settings name npm, never pnpm or yarn; any other added file or side effect of the gate (for example a marker file make check writes) is named in the final message with the reason the repository needs it

The final message is accurate about what was verified: it says CI itself was not run, it says whether the new hooks were exercised by real git commits or pushes or only by direct invocation, and it claims no check as passing that it did not run. (Whether the run committed is judged by the uncommitted-edit expectation, not here.)
No file written or edited contains an em dash character, except a hook or script that uses the character (or its escape) only as the pattern it rejects

evals.name: adopt-two-service-repo
evals.prompt: This repo has none of our conventions yet. Set it up like our other repos: AGENTS.md with CLAUDE.md importing it, a Makefile where `make check` is the same gate CI runs, and our git hooks. Keep whatever the team already relies on working.
evals.expected_output: A root Makefile whose make check runs the api CI job (a gofmt check that fails on unformatted files, go vet, go test inside services/api, since there is no root go.mod) and the worker CI job (pytest with integration deselected: 3 run, 1 deselected) and passes offline on this machine; the integration test stays reachable through its own target or CI, never points at the staging database, and how to run it locally is written down without the stale `docker compose up db` step (there is no compose file); AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (with @AGENTS.md) describe both services and the repository's own `<area>: <summary>` commit format; the pre-commit framework hook in .git/hooks keeps running with its configured hooks intact, the documented setup path does not switch it off, `pre-commit install` still works or its breakage is named, any active pre-push passes on this machine, and no hook the run writes rejects the team's subjects or its direct commits on main without saying so; the tracked services/worker/.env is reported for rotation and untracking without printing any value or rewriting history; the wrong README test commands are fixed or reported; any CI change is named and still runs in the job images; only the requested pieces are added; nothing is committed.
expectations: A Makefile exists at the repository root and `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository offline, with DATABASE_URL unset and no Postgres running; it runs the worker's tests the way the worker CI job does, with the integration marker deselected (3 tests pass, test_can_reach_postgres deselected), so the gate neither fails nor reports failure for want of a database. On this machine `python3` has no pytest while the `pytest` on PATH works; the grader first runs plain `make check`, and only if that fails for want of pytest does it rerun with an override (such as PYTHON=...) that the final message or AGENTS.md documents for exactly this case, which then counts as a pass

`make check` runs the api job's checks inside services/api (a gofmt check, go vet and go test), not `go test ./...` from the repository root, which fails there because the only go.mod is services/api/go.mod

The gofmt check in `make check` fails on an unformatted file, as CI's `test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"` does: the grader adds a badly indented .go file under services/api/internal/route and `make check` exits non-zero (plain `gofmt -l` exits 0 whatever it lists, so a recipe that only runs it passes)
The integration test is not silently dropped: a separate Makefile target runs it (with DATABASE_URL required), or the final message says make check leaves it to the worker-integration CI job
Nothing the run adds (Makefile targets, docs, AGENTS.md) points tests or commands at the staging database in services/worker/.env or reads that file

The agent instructions (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or the README) say how to run the integration test locally: a Postgres the engineer starts and DATABASE_URL pointed at it, never the staging database in services/worker/.env

The agent instructions and anything else the run writes do not tell the engineer to run `docker compose up db` or use a compose service (the repository has no compose file; the comment in services/worker/tests/test_db_integration.py is stale), and the final message or the docs note that this comment names a compose setup the repository does not have

AGENTS.md exists at the repository root and describes both services, services/api in Go and services/worker in Python, with how to check each; it is not written for one stack only. CLAUDE.md exists and contains a line that is exactly `@AGENTS.md` (a markdown link does not import)

The agent instructions (AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md) give the repository's own commit format from CONTRIBUTING.md, `<area>: <summary>` with area api, worker, ci or docs and no ticket id in the subject, and do not prescribe a different convention

Every commit-msg hook or commit-message check the run writes, whether or not git runs it yet, accepts every subject in the fixture history and the subjects `worker: skip riders at capacity` and `api: eta endpoint with stop dwell time` (the grader runs it on a message file for each); if the run chose not to write one for that reason, the final message says so

The pre-commit framework hook the team installed still runs: either core.hooksPath is left unset so .git/hooks/pre-commit keeps running, or the hooks directory it now points at calls the pre-commit framework (or .git/hooks/pre-commit); setting core.hooksPath to a new directory that never calls it fails this. The documented setup path agrees: no setup step the run writes into README, CONTRIBUTING or AGENTS.md (for example a `make hooks` target) sets core.hooksPath to a directory that bypasses the framework. The gofmt and ruff hooks in .pre-commit-config.yaml are still there and unchanged

Every pre-push hook the run writes, active or not, accepts what the team does today (every commit in the history is straight on main with no merge commits): no refusal of pushes from main, no task-id branch names, no terminal confirmation, no refusal of a push that sends no new commits. If git on this clone runs a pre-push hook the run wrote, it also exits 0 on this machine when the grader invokes it as git would for a push of main to origin/main with nothing new to send, with no extra environment variables set (a pre-push that runs make check and fails here for want of pytest refuses every push). Any refusal outside this is acceptable only if the final message names it as a change the team must agree to before it is switched on

The final message flags that services/worker/.env is tracked in git, that whatever credentials it holds should be rotated, and that it should be untracked and ignored; it repeats no value from the file (it need not read the file)
The run does not rewrite history to remove services/worker/.env and does not delete the local file; untracking it with git rm --cached and ignoring it, left uncommitted, is acceptable

The README's test instructions (`go test ./...` and `pytest` from the repository root, which fail: no root go.mod, and plain pytest runs the integration test) are corrected to commands that work, or the final message reports that they fail

.gitlab-ci.yml still runs the same three jobs with the same checks (unchanged, or calling make targets that run the same commands); no job is removed and the integration job is not weakened. If the run changed .gitlab-ci.yml at all, the final message names the change and why, and every job still runs in its own image (golang:1.25, python:3.12) without a tool or variable that image or job does not provide

services/api/go.mod and services/worker/pyproject.toml gain no dependency, the existing .gitignore entries are all still present, the run adds no .github/ directory (the repository is hosted on GitLab), and it makes no git commit: the history still ends at the fixture commit and the final message leaves the commit to the engineer

The final message says what it did not run (at least the integration test, which needs a reachable Postgres and opens a connection to it, and the pre-commit framework, which is not installed on this machine) and claims neither as passing

The run adds nothing the request did not ask for beyond what those pieces need: no SECURITY.md, .editorconfig, docs/ templates, issue or merge request templates, and no CODEOWNERS with placeholder owners such as @lead or @engineering; any other extra file is named in the final message with the reason
No file written or edited contains an em dash character, except a hook or script that uses the character (or its escape) only as the pattern it rejects

The team's documented hook setup still works after the run: CONTRIBUTING.md installs hooks with `pre-commit install`, which refuses to run while core.hooksPath is set. If the run sets core.hooksPath in this clone's git config, or writes a setup step (Makefile target, README, AGENTS.md) that sets it, the final message says that `pre-commit install` will now refuse and what teammates run instead; a run that leaves core.hooksPath unset passes this
